study: Guida (2025) Machine Learning in Commodity Futures: replication on Chinese commodity futures

sample.warmup_and_training_only: 2010-2015: features and training labels only; the backtest starts 2016-01-04
sample.sample_change: first run used 2013-2021 as the test window; corrected to the project research period 2016-2021 before any further analysis

continuous_series: RiceQuant get_dominant rank1/rank2; daily return = same-contract close-to-close, so roll days carry no price gap (ratio back-adjustment)

definitions.MOM: L-day cumulative return of rank1 series
definitions.TSMOM: L-day log return divided by (L-day daily log-return std * sqrt(L))
definitions.CARRY: L-day mean of RiceQuant main_sub annualized roll yield (positive = backwardation)
definitions.BASISMOM: L-day log return of rank1 leg minus L-day log return of rank2 leg
definitions.IVOL: L-day residual volatility against the equal-weight return of eligible symbols
definitions.MA: back-adjusted price divided by its L-day mean, minus 1
definitions.RSI: 100 * mean gain / (mean gain + mean loss) of daily returns over L days
definitions.MAV: log of total open interest over its L-day mean

features.normalization: cross-sectional percentile rank within the eligible universe on each date

targets.definition: cumulative rank1 return from close t to close t+H, cross-sectional percentile rank
targets.note: paper text lists 80d but its tables report 88d; 88d is used

model.selection: minimum validation MSE; validation = last 121 feature dates of the training window whose H-day labels are fully realized by the window end
model.retrain: annually at year end on an expanding window starting 2010
model.purge: training-part rows need t+H before the validation start; validation and final-refit rows need t+H no later than the last trading day of the window
model.final_fit: refit on the full window with the selected parameters
model.seed_deviation: paper averages 20 seeds; 5 seeds here to bound compute

portfolio.score: cross-sectional percentile of the prediction, centered at 0.5
portfolio.legs: long above median, short below median, weights proportional to |score - 0.5|, each leg gross 1
portfolio.ensemble: mean of the eight horizon percentiles, re-ranked

execution.main: weights from close t earn the return from close t to close t+1 (paper timing)
execution.robustness: one-day delay: weights from close t earn close t+1 to close t+2

portfolio.turnover: sum |w_t - w_{t-1}| plus 2|w| on each held symbol's dominant-contract roll day
portfolio.baseline_signs: set from the literature before results; not re-estimated

hypotheses_from_paper: H1: net performance by horizon is a mirror-J: highest at 5d/10d, lowest around 44-88d, rising toward 200d
H2: the ensemble has lower volatility and turnover than single horizons with Sharpe in the upper range
H3: mid horizons (22d-100d) are highly correlated with each other; 200d is the least correlated
H4: TSMOM and MOM rank among the most important features; SKEW is more important at short horizons; RSI, MA and MAV rank low
reporting: report every horizon, the ensemble, both timings, gross and net, and all baselines, including null and adverse results
